title: A Seasonal Emerald in the Sahel
caption: Natural-color MODIS composite of the Inner Niger Delta in Mali in November 2021, when seasonal floodwaters turn the wetland green where the Sahara meets the Sahel. Depending on upstream rainfall, the delta typically floods from roughly August to December.
credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Joshua Stevens, using data from the Level-1 and Atmosphere Archive & Distribution System (LAADS) and Land Atmosphere Near real-time Capability for EOS (LANCE), Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey.

title: Cultivating Egypt’s Desert
caption: Landsat 8 natural-color view of center-pivot irrigated fields at East Oweinat, a land-reclamation area in Egypt’s hyper-arid Western Desert. Each circle is a field watered by a sprinkler arm rotating around a central pivot and supplied with groundwater.
credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Joshua Stevens, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey.

title: Agriculture on the Ethiopian Plateau
caption: Astronaut photograph of densely packed smallholder fields on slightly higher ground beside floodplains and wetlands near Lake Tana in the Ethiopian Highlands. Taken at the end of the dry season, it shows mostly fallow rain-fed fields in brown and tan, with narrow fields lining the Gilgel Abbay River.
credit: Astronaut photograph ISS050-E-30105 was acquired on January 2, 2017, with a Nikon D4 digital camera using an 1150 millimeter lens, and is provided by the ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility and the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Johnson Space Center. The image was taken by a member of the Expedition 50 crew.

title: Drought in Eastern Africa
caption: Vegetation anomaly map of Africa and the Middle East for February 2006, derived from SPOT satellite vegetation data after East Africa’s 2005 short rains failed. Brown marks vegetation far less abundant or healthy than the 1998–2006 average; green marks above-normal vegetation.
credit: NASA image created by Jesse Allen, using data provided courtesy of Jennifer Small, NASA GIMMS Group at Goddard Space Flight Center.

title: As a Himalayan Glacier Melts, a Lake Grows
caption: Landsat 8 image of the Kokthang glacier in the Sikkim Himalaya, India, on 18 November 2018. Over the preceding three decades the glacier retreated and a nearby glacial lake roughly doubled in size.
credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey.

title: Global Views of ICESat-2 Data
caption: Two hemispheric globes combining ICESat-2 data products: vegetation height, terrain height, sea surface height, sea-ice height above the ocean, and land-ice height change since January 2020. Together they illustrate the laser altimeter’s measurements of land, ice, oceans and forests.
credit: NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio. Data visualizer: Kel Elkins (Science and Technology Corporation).

title: Soil Moisture Around the World
caption: Global map of moisture in the top 5 centimeters of soil from SMAP radar and radiometer observations over 27–31 May 2015, at about 9 km resolution. Deserts appear pale yellow, while rainforests, boreal forests and vegetated mountains show wetter soils.
credit: NASA Earth Observatory map by Joshua Stevens, using data courtesy of JPL and the SMAP science team.

title: An Oasis of Green in Senegal
caption: Landsat 8 view of the Senegal River Delta wetlands around Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary, on the Senegal–Mauritania border, on 14 November 2023. The delta’s lakes, lagoons and floodplains form a green refuge amid dry surroundings, with water flows now managed by dams, embankments and canals.

title: Global Vegetation
caption: Global Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from Terra MODIS averaged over 1 November to 1 December 2007. Dark greens show land with abundant leafy vegetation, beige to white shows little or none, and water appears blue.

title: Measuring Carbon and Trees in the Tropics
caption: Map of carbon stored in tree biomass across tropical Asia, New Guinea and northern Australia around the year 2000, from a benchmark pantropical forest-carbon map. The map combined ICESat GLAS lidar, MODIS, QuikSCAT and SRTM data with thousands of ground-based forest plots.
